name: DS1307 real-time clock module (Tiny RTC)
description: Maxim/Analog Devices DS1307 battery-backed I2C real-time clock: seconds to year in BCD (leap years to 2100), 56 bytes of RAM and a programmable square-wave pin. The chip needs a 4.5-5.5 V supply. The module also carries an AT24C32 EEPROM at 0x50 and a coin-cell holder. Sold as: Tiny RTC I2C module (DS1307 + AT24C32), 7-pin header P1: SQ, DS, SCL, SDA, VCC, GND, BAT; I2C address 0x68.
eli5: A little clock with its own battery that keeps the date and time even when your board is switched off.

pins.name: SQ
pins.description: SQW/OUT: open-drain square-wave (1 Hz-32 kHz) or logic output; needs a pull-up if used

pins.name: DS
pins.description: Data pin of the optional DS18B20 footprint (usually not fitted); not part of the clock

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, 100 kHz max (pull-up to VCC fitted on the module)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (pull-up to VCC fitted on the module)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 5 V (4.5-5.5 V); the DS1307 does not run from 3.3 V

pins.name: BAT
pins.description: Backup cell + (from the on-board holder); leave unconnected

supplierQuery: Tiny RTC DS1307 I2C module AT24C32
buildNotes: Power VCC from 5 V (ESP32 VIN/5V, Pico VBUS): the DS1307 needs 4.5-5.5 V and below about 1.25 x the cell voltage it stops answering on I2C.

The module pulls SDA and SCL up to VCC (5 V). ESP32 and Pico pins are not 5 V tolerant: remove the module's two I2C pull-up resistors and use 3.3 V pull-ups (4.7 kOhm), or use a level shifter. The DS1307 reads 2.2 V as high, so 3.3 V logic works.
Use I2C at 100 kHz: the DS1307 is a standard-mode-only device.
After first power-up the clock is halted (CH bit 7 of register 0x00 = 1). Setting the time writes seconds with CH = 0, which starts it.
Time registers 0x00-0x06 are BCD: seconds, minutes, hours, weekday (1-7, user-defined), date, month, year (00-99). Hour bit 6 = 1 selects 12-hour mode.
The Tiny RTC charges its cell through a diode: fit a rechargeable LIR2032, or remove the charging parts before fitting a CR2032. Without a cell, VBAT must be grounded.
The AT24C32 EEPROM on the same bus answers at 0x50; it is not modelled here.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ds1307 import DS1307

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
rtc = DS1307(i2c)
rtc.datetime((2027, 2, 28, 7, 23, 59, 57))  # Sunday 28 Feb 2027, 23:59:57 (weekday 1 = Monday)
while True:
    y, mo, d, wd, h, mi, s = rtc.datetime()
    print('wd=%d %04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d' % (wd, y, mo, d, h, mi, s))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Keeps the time it was set to and rolls over to 1 March
